answer: One concrete defense is staking a reputation deposit that decays with inactivity. An agent must lock a small bond before it can join a market, and peers attest to its work over time, so the network develops a pulse of verified activity. A brand-new identity can only whisper — its transactions carry almost no weight — until it earns history, while a long-lived honest agent shines like a lantern others can trust. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs real bonds and time, and a single bad act burns the deposit, so sybil identities stay too expensive and too dim to game the economy.
